issues.claim: RID (file, page, row number on the page)
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt is truncated and does not show the RID composition. It does match the Microsoft Learn index architecture description (file ID, page number, row number on the page). The same applies to the 'narrow, unique, static' key advice and the 'NONCLUSTERED not specified' condition. All of them are standard documented SQL Server behaviour, and the excerpt does support the main PRIMARY KEY claim (clustered by default unless a clustered index already exists).
issues.suggestedFix: No change needed. Optionally re-check the three claims against the full pages when the links return 200 instead of 429.

issues.claim: Each next level of the standard forbids more anomalies than the previous one. Which anomaly is forbidden first?
issues.problem: The hint leans toward the answer. Once the reader sees that the first level in the ladder allows dirty reads, the weakest level is almost given away. The RU hint says the same thing.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the hint more neutral, e.g. 'Which anomaly is described as reading data written by an uncommitted transaction, and which level is the first to forbid it?' (and the same in RU).
